MetaData.Value: A Certificate of Liability Insurance (COI) is a document that provides proof that a business or individual has liability insurance coverage. It summarizes key details of the policy, including: - Policyholder Information: Name and contact details of the insured. - Insurance Provider: The company issuing the policy. - Coverage Types: General liability, professional liability, workers' compensation, etc. - Policy Limits: Maximum amount the insurer will pay for claims. - Effective & Expiration Dates: The duration of coverage. Businesses often need a COI when working with clients, vendors, or landlords who require proof of insurance before entering into contracts. If you need one, you can request it from your insurance provider
